cnd22:2.1: I shall recite the Way to the Far Shore: I shall recite what was sung, retell what was told, repeat what was spoken, reiterate what was uttered, restate what was said—
cnd22:2.4: Iccā: this is a joining of words … a sequence of words—
cnd22:2.6: Venerable: this is an affectionate expression, a respectful expression, a form of address that conveys reverence and deference—
cnd22:2.8: Piṅgiya: this is the name of that elder—his designation, appellation, description, usage, name, naming, title, expression, term, and utterance—
cnd22:3.1: Yathāddakkhi tathākkhāsi: as he saw, so he stated, explained, taught, declared, established, disclosed, analyzed, made plain, and revealed it.
cnd22:3.2: “All conditions are impermanent”: as he saw, so he stated, explained, taught, declared, established, disclosed, analyzed, made plain, and revealed it.
cnd22:3.5: “everything that has the nature to arise has the nature to cease”: as he saw, so he stated, explained, taught, declared, established, disclosed, analyzed, made plain, and revealed it—
cnd22:4.2: Immaculate: greed is a stain, hate is a stain, delusion is a stain, anger is a stain …
cnd22:4.3: resentment … all unskillful volitional formations are stains.
cnd22:4.4: Those stains have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:4.5: The Buddha is stainless, immaculate, free of stain, one whose stains have departed, one who has given up stains, one who is freed from stains, one who has transcended all stains.
cnd22:4.7: The Blessed One is endowed with that wisdom—ample and broad, equal to the earth.
cnd22:4.9: The wisdom that is understanding … non-delusion, investigation of principles, right view.
cnd22:4.10: The Blessed One is possessed of, fully possessed of, has come to, has fully come to, is endowed with, is fully endowed with, and is provided with this intelligence, this wisdom; therefore the Buddha is of fine intelligence—
cnd22:5.6: For the Buddha, the Blessed One, sensual pleasures as objects are fully understood and sensual pleasures as corruptions are given up, because sensual pleasures as objects are fully understood and sensual pleasures as corruptions are given up.
cnd22:5.7: The Blessed One does not desire sensual pleasures, does not wish for sensual pleasures, does not aspire to sensual pleasures, does not long for sensual pleasures, and does not covet sensual pleasures.
cnd22:5.8: Those who desire sensual pleasures, wish for sensual pleasures, aspire to sensual pleasures, long for sensual pleasures, and covet sensual pleasures are lovers of sensual desire, those impassioned through greed, perceivers of perceptions.
cnd22:5.9: The Blessed One does not desire sensual pleasures, does not wish for sensual pleasures, does not aspire to sensual pleasures, does not long for sensual pleasures, and does not covet sensual pleasures.
cnd22:5.10: Therefore the Buddha is free of sensual desire, rid of sensual desire, one who has relinquished sensual desire, spewed it out, released it, given it up, and let it go; he is free of greed, with greed gone, one who has relinquished greed, spewed it out, released it, given it up, and let it go; he is free of hunger, extinguished, cooled, experiencing bliss, and he lives with a self that has become divine—
cnd22:6.1: Unentangled: greed is an entanglement, hate is an entanglement, delusion is an entanglement, anger is an entanglement, resentment is an entanglement …
cnd22:6.3: Those entanglements have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:6.4: Therefore the Buddha is without entanglement, free of entanglement, unentangled, one who has gone from entanglement, one who has given up entanglement, one who is freed from entanglement, one who has transcended all entanglement—
cnd22:6.7: the Blessed One does no wrong, so he is a nāga; he does not go, so he is a nāga; he does not come, so he is a nāga … in this way the Blessed One does not come, so he is a nāga—
cnd22:7.2: For what reason: for what reason, with what cause, on what grounds, from what source, by what condition—
cnd22:7.4: Would speak falsely: he might speak falsely, utter it, expound it, or express it;
cnd22:7.5: would speak falsely: he might tell a falsehood, he might speak lies, he might speak ignobly.
cnd22:7.6: Take someone here who has gone before a council, a gathering, among relatives, in the midst of a guild, or in the midst of a royal court, and, being brought forward, is questioned as a witness—
cnd22:7.7: “Come, good man, say what you know,”
cnd22:7.12: So whether for his own sake, or for another’s sake, or for some trifling material gain, he knowingly speaks falsely; this is called a falsehood.
cnd22:8.11: “I have spoken falsely,” having concealed his view—
cnd22:8.20: “I have spoken falsely,” having concealed his view, having concealed his acceptance, having concealed his preference, having concealed his perception, having concealed his inner state—
cnd22:8.21: in these eight ways there is lying, which is a falsehood.
cnd22:8.22: For what reason might he speak falsely, utter it, expound it, or express it—
cnd22:11.2: Stain: greed is a stain, hate is a stain, delusion is a stain, conceit is a stain, views are a stain, corruption is a stain, all misconduct is a stain, all deeds that lead to existence are a stain.
cnd22:12.1: Delusion: that which is ignorance regarding suffering … the crossbar of ignorance, delusion, an unskillful root.
cnd22:12.3: Both stain and delusion have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:13.17: he gives rise to conceit, thinking himself a gainer of agreeable sights,
cnd22:13.57: Take someone here who gives rise to conceit because of birth, or lineage, or being from a good family, or good looks, or wealth, or education, or occupation, or craft, or field of knowledge, or learning, or eloquence, or some other thing.
cnd22:13.58: Such conceit as this: conceiving, the state of having conceived, haughtiness, arrogance, a banner, self-assertion, a yearning to raise a flag of the mind—
cnd22:14.1: Contempt: whatever contempt, disparagement, state of disparaging, harshness, harsh action—
cnd22:14.3: Both conceit and contempt have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:15.1: Come, I shall extol with speech connected with praise.
cnd22:15.2: Handāhaṁ: this is a joining of words, a combining of words, a completion of words, a coming together of syllables, a smoothness of phrasing, and a sequence of words—
cnd22:15.4: I shall extol with speech connected with praise: speech, voice, mode of expression, and utterance that is possessed of praise, fully possessed of it, come to it, fully come to it, endowed with it, fully endowed with it, and provided with it—I shall extol, teach, declare, establish, disclose, analyze, make plain, and reveal it—
cnd22:15.5: Come, I shall extol with speech connected with praise.
cnd22:18.2: Dispeller of darkness: he drove out, drove away, abandoned, dispelled, eliminated, and annihilated the darkness of greed, the darkness of hate, the darkness of delusion, the darkness of conceit, the darkness of views, the darkness of corruptions, and the darkness of misconduct—the darkness that makes one blind, that makes one ignorant, that obstructs wisdom, that takes the side of vexation, and that does not lead to extinguishment.
cnd22:18.3: Buddha: he who is that Blessed One … is a designation arising from realization;
cnd22:18.5: All-seer is said to be the knowledge of omniscience …
cnd22:19.6: the world of existence in success and the world of origination in success;
cnd22:19.7: the world of existence in failure and the world of origination in failure.
cnd22:19.28: Gone to the world’s end: the Blessed One has gone to the end of the world, reached the end, gone to the limit, reached the limit … gone to extinguishment, reached extinguishment.
cnd22:19.29: He has lived out the life, practiced the conduct … the wandering on through birth and death; for him there is no further rebirth—
cnd22:20.3: existence as action, and renewed existence involving rebirth-linking.
cnd22:20.5: The meritorious formation, the demeritorious formation, the imperturbable formation—
cnd22:20.8: The form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness that belong to rebirth-linking—
cnd22:20.10: The Blessed One has surmounted, passed beyond, and transcended existence as action and renewed existence involving rebirth-linking—
cnd22:21.3: the defilement of sensuality, the defilement of existence, the defilement of views, the defilement of ignorance.
cnd22:21.4: Those defilements have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:21.6: Given up all suffering: all suffering of his that is linked to rebirth—the suffering of birth, the suffering of old age, the suffering of illness, the suffering of death, the suffering of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress …
cnd22:21.7: the suffering of loss of view has been given up, completely cut off, calmed, stilled, made unable to arise again, and burned by the fire of knowledge.
cnd22:22.2: Rightly named: of true appellation, of similar name, of similar appellation, of an appellation similar to the true.
cnd22:22.3: The Blessed One Vipassī, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Blessed One Vessabhū, the Blessed One Kakusandha, the Blessed One Koṇāgamana, the Blessed One Kassapa.
cnd22:22.4: Those Buddhas, those Blessed Ones, are of similar name and of similar appellation.
cnd22:22.5: The Blessed One, the Sakyan sage, too is of similar name and similar appellation to those Buddhas, those Blessed Ones—
cnd22:23.1: Revered by me, brahmin: that Blessed One has been sat close to, revered, waited upon, questioned, and queried by me—
cnd22:25.4: like a swan that has reached the great ocean.
cnd22:26.1: Like a bird that, leaving a little copse behind, would dwell in a forest abounding in fruit.
cnd22:26.4: Because it is born twice, it is a dija: once from the mother’s womb and once from the eggshell.
cnd22:26.7: Like leaving behind a little copse: just as a bird, having left behind, abandoned, passed beyond, fully passed beyond, and gone past a little copse—a small grove with little fruit, little food, and little water—might reach, find, and obtain another great forest, a wooded thicket with abundant fruit, abundant food, and abundant water, and might make its home in that wooded thicket—
cnd22:26.8: like a bird that, leaving a little copse behind, would dwell in a forest abounding in fruit.
cnd22:27.1: In the same way, having left behind those of narrow vision, I have come to the great ocean like a swan.
cnd22:27.3: Having left behind those of narrow vision: both the brahmin Bāvarī and those other teachers of his, in comparison with the Buddha, the Blessed One, are of narrow vision, of small vision, of slight vision, of inferior vision, of base vision, or of wretched vision.
cnd22:27.4: Having left behind, abandoned, passed beyond, fully passed beyond, and gone past those of narrow vision, small vision, slight vision, inferior vision, base vision, and wretched vision, I have reached, found, and obtained the Buddha, the Blessed One—of immeasurable vision, foremost vision, best vision, distinguished vision, chief vision, highest vision, and finest vision; the unequaled, the peer of the unequaled, the matchless, the one without counterpart, the one without rival; the god above the gods, the bull among men, the lion among men, the nāga among men, the thoroughbred among men, the chief bull among men, the bearer of the burden among men, the one who holds the ten powers.
cnd22:27.5: Just as a swan might reach, find, and obtain the great Lake Mānasaka, or the lake Anotatta, or the great ocean—a mass of water unstirred and measureless—in the same way I have reached, found, and obtained the Buddha, the Blessed One: unshaken, of measureless brilliance, of penetrating knowledge, with eyes unveiled, skilled in analyzing wisdom, who has attained the textual analyses, reached the four kinds of self-assurance, whose resolve is pure, whose inner being is spotless, who speaks without duplicity, who is unmoved, who does as he declares, not small but great, deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, rich in jewels, like the ocean, endowed with the equanimity of six factors, incomparable, vast, and boundless—such a one among speakers, among proclaimers of the path, like Meru among mountains, like the garuḷa among birds, like the lion among beasts, like the ocean among seas; I have reached him, that Teacher, the foremost of Victors, the great seer—
cnd22:27.6: In the same way, having left behind those of narrow vision, I have come to the great ocean like a swan.
cnd22:30.2: Those who: both the brahmin Bāvarī and those other teachers of his answered, explained, taught, declared, established, disclosed, analyzed, made plain, and revealed their own view, their own acceptance, their own preference, their own doctrine, their own inclination, and their own intention—
cnd22:31.1: Before Gotama’s teaching: previous to Gotama’s teaching, outside Gotama’s teaching, prior to Gotama’s teaching, earlier than Gotama’s teaching, than the Buddha’s teaching, than the Victor’s teaching, than the Realized One’s teaching, than the teaching of the perfected ones—
cnd22:32.1: It was so, it will be so: they say it was so, they say it will be so—
cnd22:33.1: All that was just hearsay: all that was just hearsay, by testament, by lineage, by canonical authority, by logic, by inference, by a reasoned train of thought, by acceptance of a view after deliberation; the teaching that they spoke of was not directly known by themselves, not witnessed personally—
cnd22:34.1: All that fostered speculation: all that fostered speculation, fostered thought, fostered intention, fostered sensual thought, fostered thoughts of malice, fostered thoughts of cruelty, fostered thoughts about relatives, fostered thoughts about the country, fostered thoughts about immortality, fostered thoughts connected with sympathy for others, fostered thoughts connected with gain, honor, and fame, fostered thoughts connected with not being looked down on—
cnd22:37.2: Alone: the Blessed One is alone through what is called going forth; alone in the sense of having no second; alone in the sense of giving up craving; alone as one entirely free of greed; alone as one entirely free of hate; alone as one entirely free of delusion; alone as one entirely free of corruptions; alone as one who has gone on the one-way path; alone as one who alone has awakened to the supreme perfect awakening.
cnd22:38.2: When the Blessed One was still young, a lad with jet-black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, against the wishes of his weeping and wailing mother and father, whose faces were wet with tears, he cut off the circle of relatives and every impediment of household life; he cut off the impediment of wife and children, the impediment of relatives, the impediment of friends and colleagues, and the impediment of hoarding; he shaved off his hair and beard, put on ocher robes, went forth from the lay life to homelessness, and reached the state of owning nothing; alone he lives, dwells, conducts himself, proceeds, maintains himself, sustains himself, and keeps going.
cnd22:39.2: Having gone forth in this way, alone he frequents remote lodgings in wilderness and forest—those with little sound and little noise, free of the breath of crowds, fit for private human affairs, and suitable for retreat.
cnd22:39.3: He goes alone, stands alone, sits alone, lies down alone, enters the village for alms alone, advances alone, returns alone, sits in private alone, takes up walking meditation alone; alone he lives, dwells, conducts himself, proceeds, maintains himself, sustains himself, and keeps going.
cnd22:40.1: How is the Blessed One alone in the sense of giving up craving?
cnd22:40.2: Being alone in this way, with no second, diligent, keen, and resolute, as he stayed on the bank of the river Nerañjarā at the foot of the Bodhi tree and made the great effort, he routed Māra with his army—the Dark One, Namuci, kinsman of the negligent—and abandoned, dispelled, eliminated, and annihilated craving with its net, wide-spread and clinging.
cnd22:44.2: Because greed is given up, he is alone as one entirely free of greed; because hate is given up, he is alone as one entirely free of hate; because delusion is given up, he is alone as one entirely free of delusion; because corruptions are given up, he is alone as one entirely free of corruptions.
cnd22:45.1: How is the Blessed One alone as one who has gone on the one-way path?
cnd22:45.2: The one-way path is said to be the four kinds of mindfulness meditation …
cnd22:48.1: How is the Blessed One alone as the one who alone has awakened to the supreme perfect awakening?
cnd22:48.2: Awakening is said to be the knowledge, wisdom, faculty of wisdom, power of wisdom, awakening factor of investigation of principles, inquiry, discernment, and right view in the four paths.
cnd22:48.3: With that knowledge of awakening, the Blessed One awakened to “All conditions are impermanent”,
cnd22:48.6: he awakened to “everything that has the nature to arise has the nature to cease”.
cnd22:48.7: Or else, whatever was to be awakened to, understood, comprehended, fully awakened to, attained, touched, and realized, all that he awakened to, understood, comprehended, fully awakened to, attained, touched, and realized with that knowledge of awakening.
cnd22:48.8: In this way the Blessed One alone fully awakened to the supreme perfect awakening, and so is alone.
cnd22:49.1: Dispeller of darkness: the Blessed One drove out, drove away, abandoned, dispelled, eliminated, and annihilated the darkness of greed, the darkness of hate, the darkness of delusion, the darkness of views, the darkness of corruptions, and the darkness of misconduct—the darkness that makes one blind, that makes one eyeless, that makes one ignorant, that obstructs wisdom, that takes the side of vexation, and that does not lead to extinguishment.
cnd22:49.2: Seated: the Blessed One is seated at the Pāsāṇaka Shrine—
cnd22:51.2: or else, because all exertions have been stilled, the Blessed One is seated: he has lived out the life, practiced the conduct … the wandering on through birth and death; for him there is no further rebirth; in this way too the Blessed One is seated—
cnd22:52.2: Brilliant: brilliant, thoughtful, astute, wise, sagacious, knowing, discerning, and intelligent.
cnd22:52.3: A beacon: a beacon, a bringer of light, one who makes things shine, a lamp-maker, a lamp-lighter, one who illuminates, one who makes things blaze—

cnd22:56.4: The wisdom that is understanding … non-delusion, investigation of principles, right view.

cnd22:60.3: Or else, whoever develops the noble eightfold path in this very life—straight after that path, without a gap, they attain the fruit for sure, find it, and obtain it; in this way too it is apparent in the present life.

cnd22:89.1: I see him with my mind as if with my eyes: just as a person with eyes, in the light, might see, behold, look at, contemplate, and examine visible things, in the same way I see, behold, look at, contemplate, and examine the Buddha, the Blessed One, with my mind—
cnd22:90.1: Night and day, brahmin, diligent: developing recollection of the Buddha with the mind by night and by day, one is diligent—
cnd22:91.2: Paying homage: paying homage with the body, or paying homage with speech, or paying homage with the mind, or paying homage by practice in line with the meaning, or paying homage by practice in line with the teaching, honoring, respecting, esteeming, and venerating him, I pass, spend, and get through the night and day—
cnd22:92.1: Hence I think there is no separation: developing that recollection of the Buddha, I consider it non-separation; I consider that I am not apart from him; I consider it, and I know it.
cnd22:92.2: Thus I know, thus I understand, thus I discern, thus I recognize, thus I penetrate—
cnd22:95.1: Faith and joy and mind and mindfulness.
cnd22:95.2: Faith: whatever faith there is concerning the Blessed One—trust, confidence, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, the power of faith.
cnd22:95.3: Joy: whatever joy there is concerning the Blessed One—joy, delight, rejoicing, gladness, great gladness, mirth, hilarity, satisfaction, contentment, elation, and happiness of mind.
cnd22:95.4: Mind: whatever thought there is concerning the Blessed One—thought, mind, mentation, heart, the pure, mind, the mind sense base, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind consciousness.
cnd22:95.5: Mindfulness: whatever mindfulness there is concerning the Blessed One—mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness—
cnd22:96.1: These do not stray from Gotama’s teaching: these four things do not depart from, go away from, abandon, or lose Gotama’s teaching, the Buddha’s teaching, the Victor’s teaching, the Realized One’s teaching, the teaching of the perfected ones—
cnd22:97.1: Whichever direction the one of vast wisdom goes.
cnd22:97.2: Whichever direction: he goes, travels, steps, and strides toward the eastern direction, or the western direction, or the southern direction, or the northern direction.
cnd22:97.3: Vast in wisdom: vast in wisdom, of great wisdom, sharp wisdom, broad wisdom, joyful wisdom, swift wisdom, and penetrating wisdom.
cnd22:97.5: The Blessed One is endowed with that wisdom—ample and broad, equal to the earth—
cnd22:98.1: I bow in that very direction: that person bows in just that direction in which the Buddha is, leans toward it, tends toward it, slopes toward it, is committed to it, and has it as his authority—
cnd22:101.1: For me, old and feeble: old, elderly, aged, advanced in years, arrived at the stage of old age.
cnd22:101.2: Feeble: of one who is feeble in strength, of little strength, of limited strength—
cnd22:102.1: So my body cannot go there: the body does not go in the direction where the Buddha is; it does not proceed, does not go, does not pass over—
cnd22:103.1: I always go in thought: I go, travel, and cross over by going through intention, going through thought, going through knowledge, going through wisdom, going through intellect—
cnd22:104.1: For my mind, brahmin, is bound to him.
cnd22:104.2: Mind: whatever is thought, mind, mentation … the corresponding element of mind consciousness.
cnd22:104.3: For my mind, brahmin, is bound to him: the mind is bound, firmly bound, linked to the direction where the Buddha is—
cnd22:107.2: Lying in the mud: lying, sleeping, dwelling, residing, living in the mud of sensual pleasures, the mire of sensual pleasures, the corruption of sensual pleasures, the fishhook of sensual pleasures, the fever of sensual pleasures, the impediment of sensual pleasures—
cnd22:107.4: Floundering: thrashing through the thrashings of craving,
cnd22:107.30: thrashing through sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress,
cnd22:107.93: through suffering from contact with gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things …
cnd22:107.102: through the suffering of loss of view, thrashing, floundering, trembling, and shuddering—
cnd22:108.1: I drifted from island to island: from teacher to teacher, from exposition of the teaching to exposition of the teaching, from group to group, from view to view, from practice to practice, from path to path, I drifted, drifted along, and drifted about—
cnd22:109.2: Then: this is a joining of words, a combining of words, a completion of words, a coming together of syllables, a smoothness of phrasing, and a sequence of words—
cnd22:109.4: I saw: I saw, I beheld, I perceived, I penetrated.
cnd22:109.5: Buddha: that Blessed One, the self-arisen, who had no teacher …
cnd22:110.2: One who has crossed the flood: the Blessed One has crossed the flood of sensuality,
cnd22:110.6: he has crossed, crossed over, crossed completely, passed beyond, completely passed beyond, and transcended the whole path of transmigration,
cnd22:110.7: he has lived out the life, practiced the conduct … the wandering on through birth and death,
cnd22:110.11: the defilement of sensuality, the defilement of existence, the defilement of views, the defilement of ignorance.
cnd22:110.12: Those defilements have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:112.3: In the same way, you too should commit to faith,
cnd22:112.4: You will go, Piṅgiya, to the far shore of Death’s domain.
cnd22:113.1: Just as Vakkali was committed to faith, and Bhadrāvudha and Gotama of Āḷavī: just as the elder Vakkali was faithful, revered faith, had faith as his forerunner, was devoted to faith, had faith as his authority, and attained perfection; just as the elder Bhadrāvudha was faithful, revered faith, had faith as his forerunner, was devoted to faith, had faith as his authority, and attained perfection; just as the elder Āḷavigotama was faithful, revered faith, had faith as his forerunner, was devoted to faith, had faith as his authority, and attained perfection—
cnd22:113.2: just as Vakkali was committed to faith, as were Bhadrāvudha and Gotama of Āḷavī.
cnd22:114.1: In the same way, you too should commit to faith: in the same way you should entrust yourself to faith, commit to it, commit fully to it, resolve on it, and have confidence in it.
cnd22:114.2: “All conditions are impermanent”: entrust yourself to faith, commit to it, commit fully to it, resolve on it, and have confidence in it.
cnd22:114.4: “all things are not-self”: entrust yourself to faith, commit to it, commit fully to it, resolve on it, and have confidence in it …
cnd22:114.5: “everything that has the nature to arise has the nature to cease”: entrust yourself to faith, commit to it, commit fully to it, resolve on it, and have confidence in it—
cnd22:115.1: You will go, Piṅgiya, to the far shore of Death’s domain: Death’s domain is said to be the corruptions, the aggregates, and the volitional formations.
cnd22:115.2: The far shore of Death’s domain is said to be the deathless extinguishment, which is the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd22:115.3: You will go, Piṅgiya, to the far shore of Death’s domain: you will go to the far shore, you will attain the far shore, you will touch the far shore, you will realize the far shore—
cnd22:115.4: You will go, Piṅgiya, to the far shore of Death’s domain.
cnd22:116.4: You will go, Piṅgiya, to the far shore of Death’s domain.”
cnd22:118.1: Thus I grow more confident: I grow still more confident, more and more I have faith, more and more I trust, more and more I resolve;
cnd22:118.2: “all conditions are impermanent”: more and more I grow confident, more and more I have faith, more and more I trust, more and more I resolve;
cnd22:118.3: “all conditions are suffering”: more and more I grow confident …
cnd22:118.4: “all things are not-self”: more and more I grow confident …
cnd22:118.5: “everything that has the nature to arise has the nature to cease”: more and more I grow confident, more and more I have faith, more and more I trust, and more and more I resolve—
cnd22:119.2: Sage: sagacity is said to be knowledge … having gone beyond the net of ties, he is a sage.
cnd22:119.3: Hearing the words of the sage: having heard your words, speech, teaching, instruction, and counsel, having grasped, retained, and noted them—
cnd22:120.3: the veil of craving, the veil of views, the veil of corruptions, the veil of misconduct, the veil of ignorance.
cnd22:120.4: Those veils have been uncovered, demolished, and removed by the Buddha, the Blessed One; they have been given up, completely cut off, calmed, stilled, made unable to arise again, and burned by the fire of knowledge.
cnd22:120.6: Buddha: that Blessed One who … is a designation arising from realization, that is, Buddha—
cnd22:121.2: Free of barrenness: greed is barrenness, hate is barrenness, delusion is barrenness, anger is barrenness, resentment … all unskillful volitional formations are barrenness.
cnd22:121.3: Those forms of barrenness have been given up by the Buddha, the Blessed One, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.
cnd22:122.1: Eloquent: there are three who are eloquent—
cnd22:122.2: eloquent through study, eloquent through inquiry, eloquent through attainment.
cnd22:122.4: Take someone here who has learned the Buddha’s word by heart: discourses, mixed prose and verse, analyses, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, birth stories, amazing deeds, and elaborations.
cnd22:123.2: Take someone here who is a questioner about meaning, about method, about characteristics, about causes, and about what is possible and impossible.
cnd22:124.2: Take someone here who has attained the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path, the four noble paths, the four fruits of the ascetic life, the four textual analyses, and the six direct knowledges.
cnd22:124.3: For them, the meaning is known, the text is known, the definition is known.
cnd22:124.4: When the meaning is known, the meaning occurs to them; when the text is known, the text occurs to them; when the definition is known, the definition occurs to them.
cnd22:124.5: The knowledge in these three knowledges is the textual analysis of eloquence.
cnd22:124.6: The Blessed One is possessed of, fully possessed of, has come to, has fully come to, is endowed with, is fully endowed with, and is provided with this textual analysis of eloquence.
cnd22:124.8: For one who has no study, no inquiry, and no attainment, what would occur to him?—
cnd22:127.3: gods by convention, gods by rebirth, gods by purification.
cnd22:127.5: Gods by convention are said to be kings, princes, and queens.
cnd22:127.8: Gods by rebirth are said to be the gods of the Four Great Kings, the gods of the Thirty-Three … the gods of Brahmā’s host, and whichever gods are higher than that.
cnd22:127.11: Gods by purification are said to be the Realized Ones, the disciples of the Realized Ones who are perfected ones with defilements ended, and the solitary Buddhas.
cnd22:127.13: The Blessed One, having directly known the gods by convention as supreme gods, having directly known the gods by rebirth as supreme gods, having directly known the gods by purification as supreme gods, having known, weighed, judged, clarified, and made evident—
cnd22:128.1: He knew all, the higher and the lower: the Blessed One knew, understood, touched, and penetrated the principles that make supreme gods, for himself and for others.
cnd22:128.3: Right practice, practice in conformity, non-contrary practice, practice in line with the meaning, practice in line with the teaching, fulfilling ethics, guarding the sense doors, moderation in eating, dedication to wakefulness, mindfulness and situational awareness, the four kinds of mindfulness meditation … the noble eightfold path.
cnd22:128.4: These are said to be the principles that make supreme gods for oneself.
cnd22:129.2: Right practice … the noble eightfold path.
cnd22:129.3: These are said to be the principles that make supreme gods for others.
cnd22:129.4: In this way the Blessed One knew, understood, touched, and penetrated the principles that make supreme gods, for himself and for others—
cnd22:130.1: The Teacher who brings questions to an end: the Blessed One is one who ends, brings to a close, delimits, and wraps up the questions of the Way to the Far Shore;
cnd22:130.2: he is one who ends, brings to a close, delimits, and wraps up the questions of Sabhiya;
cnd22:130.15: the questions of the Brahmās, one who ends, brings to a close, delimits, and wraps up—
cnd22:130.18: Just as a caravan leader takes a caravan across a wilderness: he takes it across a wilderness of bandits, takes it across a wilderness of wild beasts, takes it across a wilderness of famine, takes it across a waterless wilderness—takes it across, takes it over, takes it out, takes it right across—and brings it to a land of safety;
cnd22:130.19: in the same way the Blessed One, the caravan leader, takes beings across the wilderness,
cnd22:130.23: takes them across the wilderness of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress,
cnd22:130.36: takes them across the thicket of misconduct—takes them across, takes them over, takes them out, takes them right across;
cnd22:131.1: Or else, the Blessed One is a leader, a guide, a conductor, one who instructs, one who gets others to reflect, one who shows, and one who inspires confidence; in this way the Blessed One is a caravan leader.
cnd22:131.2: Or else, the Blessed One is the one who gives rise to the path that had not arisen, who produces the path that had not been produced, who declares the path that had not been declared; he is one who knows the path, one who finds the path, one who is skilled in the path; and now his disciples live following the path, and come to be endowed with it afterwards; in this way too the Blessed One is a caravan leader—
cnd22:132.1: For those who admit their doubts: those who come with doubt become free of doubt; those who come with blemishes become unblemished; those who come with indecision become free of indecision; those who come with uncertainty become free of uncertainty; those who come with greed become free of greed; those who come with hate become free of hate; those who come with delusion become free of delusion; those who come with corruptions become free of corruptions—
cnd22:134.3: Surely I shall go; I have no doubt about this,
cnd22:134.4: Consider me thus, as one whose mind is resolved.
cnd22:135.1: Unfaltering: the unfaltering is said to be the deathless extinguishment.
cnd22:135.2: That which is the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd22:135.3: Unfaltering: extinguishment is not to be carried off by greed, by hate, by delusion, by anger, by resentment, by contempt, by viciousness, by jealousy, by stinginess, by deceit, by deviousness, by obstinacy, by aggression, by conceit, by arrogance, by vanity, by negligence, by all corruptions, by all misconduct, by all fevers, by all defilements, by all disturbances, by all torments, or by all unskillful volitional formations; extinguishment is permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change—
cnd22:136.1: Unshakable: the unshakable is said to be the deathless extinguishment.
cnd22:136.2: That which is the stilling of all activities … cessation, extinguishment.
cnd22:136.3: No arising of extinguishment is evident, there is no passing away, and no alteration of it is evident.
cnd22:136.4: Extinguishment is permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change—
cnd22:137.3: There is no compare: no comparison exists, no analogy exists, nothing similar exists, no counterpart exists; it does not exist, is not found, and cannot be obtained.
cnd22:137.4: Anywhere: anywhere, in anything, in any place, internally, externally, or both internally and externally—
cnd22:138.1: Surely I shall go; I have no doubt about this.
cnd22:138.2: Surely: this is a word that is definite, a word without uncertainty, a word without doubt, a word without ambiguity, a word without indecision, a word that is binding, a word that is unfailing, a word that is unerring, a word that is unwavering—
cnd22:138.4: I shall go: I shall go, attain, touch, and realize—
cnd22:138.7: About this: in extinguishment there is no doubt, no uncertainty, no indecision, no hesitation; it does not exist, is not found, is not available; given up, completely cut off, calmed, stilled, made unable to arise again, and burned by the fire of knowledge—
cnd22:139.1: Consider me thus, as one whose mind is resolved.
cnd22:139.2: Consider me thus: recognize me thus.
cnd22:139.3: One whose mind is resolved: one who leans toward extinguishment, tends toward extinguishment, slopes toward extinguishment, is committed to extinguishment—
